messages:
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Nora Patel <nora@evalworks.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Transient buffer orchestration for eval sweeps — reserve headroom request

Hi team,

EvalWorks is planning a 48–72 hour, full-model eval sweep across a few LLM variants starting next Tuesday (early PST window). Nora expects bursts of concurrent token-level traffic for inference evals that will look like rapid short-lived spikes — mostly short sequences but heavy QPS. They asked whether we can guarantee a transient headroom window (temporary reserved GPUs) to avoid throttling and noisy autoscale behavior.

Quick asks:
- Can Product/Capacity confirm the smallest guaranteed carve-out we can provide (GPU count + region) for a 72-hour window?
- Can Ops/Runtime note any autoscale exception we need to enable (policy override, cooldown adjustments, prefix-caching constraints)?
- I attached a rough capacity estimate from the EvalWorks team and a draft runbook.

We should decide today on the number to request and whether this follows the standard temporary-reserve workflow or needs an exception path. Nora, tagging you for expected concurrency peaks and preferred proposal windows.

Thanks,
David
David Kim
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachments: eval_sweep_capacity_estimates_v1.xlsx (XLSX), transient-buffer-runbook_v0.3.md (MD)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Transient buffer orchestration for eval sweeps — reserve headroom request

David — thanks for the heads-up. A few immediate notes:

- Policy: Standard temporary reserve windows are 24/72/168 hour options. Anything above 24 hours typically requires product signoff + documented impact to the pool (so that SLA customers aren't impacted).
- Autoscale: If the workload is highly spiky, we can add an autoscale soft-lock for the reserved slice so it doesn't drain to zero during cooldowns. That requires an exception ticket (ops + infra owners) and a config change to the scale-down grace period.
- Numbers: I need a clearer QPS->GPU mapping. Laura, can you map the attached estimations to GPUs and worst-case sustained token/sec so we can propose a concrete reserve.

If this is EvalWorks' first large sweep with us, my preference is to start with a modest 4-GPU reserved slice in us-west1 for 72 hours and allow an immediate bump path if telemetry shows higher demand. That keeps risk low.

Kimberly
VP, Product Operations

Attaching a quick mapping from EvalWorks' spreadsheet to our capacity model. Summary below (full sheet attached):

- Worst-case parallel requests: 1,200 concurrent short-sequence requests (median 40 tokens).
- Estimated sustained token/sec: ~48k tokens/sec across the sweep window.
- Conservative GPU sizing (g6-standard equivalency): 1 GPU ~ 12k tokens/sec for this mix -> recommended start = 4 GPUs; safety bump to 6 GPUs if concurrency > 1.5k.

Operational constraints: prefix/KV caching won't help much for pure evals because inputs vary; batching efficiency will be low due to short sequences. So cost-per-token will be higher than typical product workloads during this sweep.

I've also sketched a short runbook for the temporary slice: how to enable the soft-lock, cooldown extension, expected alarms, and rollback steps. See transient-buffer-runbook_v0.3.md attached.

Attachments: eval_sweep_capacity_estimates_v1.xlsx (XLSX), transient-buffer-runbook_v0.3.md (MD)

Laura Bennett
Senior Capacity Planner, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Nora Patel <nora@evalworks.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Transient buffer orchestration for eval sweeps — reserve headroom request

Thanks — did a quick check with runtime metrics and kernel latency tests. Key points:

- Kernel hot paths show a slight tail-latency increase when small-batch short-sequence QPS spikes hit without prefix cache. We measured a 5–12% CPU/GPU jitter at simulated 1.2k concurrent short requests. I attached the PDF summary.
- Network: colocated slices in us-west1 are preferred for EvalWorks; cross-region spikes increase tail latencies by ~20%.
- Ops request: If we reserve a 4 GPU slice and enable soft-lock, we should also put a temporary cap on preemptible scheduling for those nodes to reduce churn; that requires an exception to the preempt policy (I can file ops ticket if we decide).

Proposal (my recommendation): Reserve 4 GPUs in us-west1 for 72 hours with soft-lock + extended cooldown, file a preemptible-exception for the slice, and keep a 48-hour escalation credit to bump to 6 GPUs if sustained concurrency exceeds threshold X (I suggest X=1,500 concurrent).

Marcus Lin
Principal Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: kernel-latency-measurements.pdf (PDF)

Team — thanks for the fast turn. Consensus summary for Exec/Procurement handoff:

- Reserve: 4 GPUs (us-west1), 72-hour window starting Tue 2026-12-21 00:00 PST.
- Exception policy: soft-lock + extended scale-down cooldown; preemptible scheduling disabled for the slice.
- Escalation: bump to 6 GPUs if concurrent > 1,500; monitoring alert to David/Laura/Marcus.
- Cost & approvals: EvalWorks has agreed to cover incremental reserved-hour charges; finance/Procurement will need the estimate and the DocuSign addendum.

Action items:
1) Kimberly — please create the product signoff doc and mark this as temporary-reserve exception.
2) Stephanie — can you open the procurement request (Deal EV-WK-2026-98) and attach the estimate? Add 48-hour approval SLA so we can commit before the sweep.
3) Marcus/Laura — file the ops ticket to disable preemptible scheduling and push the soft-lock config.
4) David — I'll coordinate the DocuSign addendum with EvalWorks; Nora will send the PO after procurement request is live.

Nora — thank you for being flexible on timing. If anything changes on your side, send a 24-hour heads-up and we'll attempt a rapid bump.

David
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
